subject: Public Administration
title: XI. Public Administration Accountability and Control

segments.text: Public authority must be answerable for its legality, conduct, use of public money, and the results it achieves — accountability is therefore central to democratic administration, not an optional add-on to it. The recommended revision tool for this entire unit is an

: internal administrative control, legislative oversight, executive oversight, judicial review, dedicated audit/oversight bodies, and citizens/media/civil society — for each, state its specific power, its method of exercising that power, and its genuine limitation.

Responsiveness means administrators genuinely recognize and react to legitimate public needs and lawful political direction, while still acting within law, professional standards, and actual institutional capacity. A precise, frequently tested caution: responsiveness is

the same as simply obeying every demand made of an official — public officials must also actively protect legality, procedural fairness, and the broader public interest, meaning genuine responsiveness sometimes requires declining an improper demand rather than complying with it.

Representative bureaucracy asks whether public organizations demographically reflect the population they serve, and whether that representation genuinely improves legitimacy, understanding of diverse public needs, and fairness. A precise distinction, frequently tested:
means the workforce’s composition demographically resembles the wider society;

asks the further, empirically separate question of whether that demographic presence actually changes decisions or outcomes in practice. The syllabus specifically cautions against assuming these two are automatically identical — a workforce can achieve passive representation (demographic resemblance) without necessarily achieving active representation (actual behavioural or decisional difference), and demonstrating awareness of this gap is precisely what distinguishes a strong answer here.

— engagement genuinely adds value only when it is inclusive (reaching beyond already-privileged or already-vocal groups), informed (participants have genuine access to relevant information), and meaningfully connected to actual decision processes (rather than being purely symbolic consultation with no real influence on the eventual decision).

blocks.text: .5 The Concept and Approaches to Public Accountability

segments.text: Accountability generally involves an obligation to explain and justify one’s conduct to a forum that can question, judge, and potentially sanction that conduct. Two core dimensions, frequently tested as a pair:
(the duty to explain and justify conduct) and

(the forum’s actual capacity to require correction or impose consequences). A complete accountability relationship requires all of the following elements together: a clearly identified actor, an applicable standard against which conduct is judged, adequate information about what actually happened, a genuine forum with standing to ask questions, and some real capacity in that forum to question conduct or act on its findings — an accountability mechanism missing any one of these elements (a forum with no real power to sanction, for instance) is correspondingly weaker even if the other elements are present.

Three distinct forms of external control, precisely distinguished:
works through law-making, budget authorization, and direct legislative oversight (committee hearings, questions to ministers);
works through internal direction, hierarchical supervision, and disciplinary authority within the administration itself;

works through review of legality and protection of constitutional rights, operating strictly within the courts’ own constitutional jurisdiction (courts generally review the legality of an administrative decision, not its underlying policy merits, echoing the judicial-review discussion in Unit VI).
Administrative corruption is the abuse of entrusted public power for improper private or political benefit. A rigorous analytical treatment separates distinct stages —

blocks.text: .9 Civil Society, Media, and Interest Groups

segments.text: These non-state actors can provide independent information, advocacy, monitoring, and sustained pressure for transparency and accountability that formal government mechanisms alone may not generate. The syllabus’s important balancing caution: these actors can also be

of the wider public (well-resourced advocacy groups may not represent marginalized populations, and media coverage may be skewed by commercial or political interests) — their accountability role should therefore be
, not idealized as an automatically neutral or comprehensive check on government.

Pakistan-specific accountability claims should be grounded in constitutional provisions, actual audit reports, ombudsman and oversight body reports, court judgments, and verified governance data — with sweeping, unsupported generalizations about specific institutions specifically avoided, consistent with the evidentiary standard applied throughout this unit.

items.text: The complete accountability relationship needs actor + standard + information + forum + capacity to act — a mechanism missing any one element is correspondingly weaker, a useful diagnostic for evaluating any specific accountability institution described in a question.
Passive representation (demographic resemblance) and active representation (actual behavioural difference) are empirically separate — do not assume one implies the other.

Legislative, executive, and judicial control are three distinct mechanisms operating through different methods (law/budget/oversight; hierarchy/discipline; legality review) — a strong answer names which specific mechanism is at work in a given accountability scenario.
